name: Plate-Loaded Viking Press
description: The plate-loaded Viking press uses a Viking press machine or landmine-based Viking press attachment, which allows the hands to press in a neutral (palms-facing) grip along a fixed arc from shoulder height to full overhead extension. The arcing path of the handles closely approximates the natural pressing pathway of a dumbbell press while allowing barbell-style loading plates, making it a shoulder-friendly alternative to the straight barbell overhead press with the loading capacity of a barbell movement.

execution.starting_position: Grip the Viking press handles with a neutral grip at shoulder height. Feet shoulder-width apart, standing in front of the machine or landmine anchor.
execution.setup_instructions: Load weight plates onto the Viking press arms evenly. Begin with moderate loads as the pressing arc is different from a straight barbell.
steps: Step 1: Begin with the handles at shoulder height, elbows bent.
Step 2: Press both handles upward and slightly forward, following the arc of the machine.
Step 3: Extend to full overhead lockout.
Step 4: Lower under control along the same arc.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before pressing. Exhale through the press.
common_mistakes: Fighting the arc — the fixed bar path is an advantage; follow it rather than trying to press straight
Locking the elbows aggressively — control the lockout
safety_considerations: The arcing pressing path is gentler on the shoulder than a straight barbell
Still requires adequate shoulder mobility for overhead pressing
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Shoulder height to full overhead lockout along the machine's arc.
coaching_cues: Follow the arc — don't fight it
